title: Photon scale converter
question: What linked energy, vacuum wavelength, equivalent mass, and equivalent temperature scales follow from one stated photon frequency?
predictionPrompt: Choose an illustrative source frequency, predict which outputs rise or fall with frequency, and name the two equivalent scales without turning them into rest-mass or thermal-state claims.
sourceRevision: PHYSICS_TOUR_MASTER_PLAN.md, 2026-07-26 contract; BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment
sourceLocator: Chapter 5 photon bridge; fixed h, c, and k_B; bounded frequency contract
caveats: Equivalent mass E_gamma/c^2 is not photon rest mass.
Equivalent temperature E_gamma/k_B is not a thermodynamic state.
No source-frequency uncertainty is supplied or propagated.

numericalMethod.name: One-frequency photon identity evaluation
numericalMethod.description: Evaluates four algebraically linked identities once for one finite frequency within the engine bounds.

modelComponents.label: Photon frequency-energy relationship
modelComponents.description: Maps a stated cyclic frequency to one-photon energy using the exact International System of Units (SI) Planck constant.

attribution.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment
attribution.sourceLocator: Fixed h and photon energy-frequency relationship
caveats: nu is cyclic frequency in hertz, not angular frequency.

modelComponents.label: Vacuum frequency-wavelength relationship
modelComponents.description: Maps the stated frequency to vacuum wavelength with exact SI c and excludes material dispersion.

attribution.sourceLocator: Fixed c and vacuum propagation relationship
caveats: Wavelength in matter requires a refractive model outside this simulation.

modelComponents.label: Energy-equivalent coordinate map
modelComponents.description: Divides the same photon energy by c squared and k_B to produce explicitly labeled equivalent mass and temperature scales.

attribution.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; tour-photon-bridge-v1 contract
attribution.sourceLocator: Equivalent mass and temperature labeling boundary
caveats: The outputs are coordinate labels, not photon rest mass or a thermal-state assignment.

assumptions: The input is a finite positive cyclic frequency within [1e3, 1e25] Hz.
The radiation is represented by one photon of the stated frequency.
The reported wavelength is a vacuum wavelength.
No input-frequency uncertainty is supplied, so no output uncertainty is reported.
Illustrative presets are source choices rather than exact spectral-band definitions.

controls.label: Photon frequency
controls.description: Supplies one cyclic frequency to the photon identity engine within its exact finite bounds.
controls.playfulPrompt: Move from radio waves toward gamma rays and predict which scale runs backward.

presets.label: Radio
presets.description: Use the engine's illustrative 100 MHz radio frequency.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Why is the vacuum wavelength macroscopic while one-photon energy is small?

presets.label: Microwave
presets.description: Use the engine's illustrative 10 GHz microwave frequency.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Which outputs scale directly with frequency, and which one scales inversely?

presets.label: Visible blue
presets.description: Use the engine's illustrative frequency corresponding to a 450 nm vacuum wavelength.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Can you state the mass and temperature outputs with equivalent labels before reading their values?

presets.label: X-ray
presets.description: Use the engine's illustrative frequency corresponding to a 0.1 nm vacuum wavelength.
presets.inspectionPrompt: How does shortening vacuum wavelength change one-photon energy?

presets.label: Gamma ray
presets.description: Use the engine's illustrative high-energy gamma-ray frequency.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Why does a large equivalent temperature still not identify a thermal state?

outputSchema.label: Frequency
outputSchema.description: The stated cyclic frequency accepted by the engine.

outputSchema.label: Vacuum wavelength
outputSchema.description: Vacuum wavelength lambda_vac = c/nu; no material refractive model is applied.

outputSchema.label: Equivalent mass scale
outputSchema.description: Energy-equivalent mass E_gamma/c^2, explicitly not photon rest mass.

outputSchema.label: Equivalent temperature scale
outputSchema.description: Energy-equivalent temperature E_gamma/k_B, explicitly not a thermodynamic state.

outputSchema.label: Relationship status
outputSchema.description: Reports exact-si-identity-for-stated-frequency while retaining the input and floating-point caveats.

comparison.incompatibleBehavior: Render frequency cases in parallel without residuals or merged equivalent scales when simulation revision or output schema differs.

visualization.description: Shows one photon frequency linked separately to photon energy, vacuum wavelength, equivalent mass scale, and equivalent temperature scale.

alternatives.description: A sentence reports all five numerical values, their equations and units, and the rest-mass, thermal-state, vacuum, and uncertainty caveats.
A table lists frequency, photon energy, vacuum wavelength, equivalent mass, and equivalent temperature with equation and interpretation columns.

visualization.reducedMotionBehavior: Render the complete linked photon scale map immediately without animated transitions between representations.

finding.changed: At runtime, the bounded frequency changes four linked representations through one direct identity evaluation.
finding.cause: Exact SI values of h, c, and k_B transform the stated frequency through photon, vacuum, and equivalent-coordinate relationships.
finding.equation: E_gamma = h nu; lambda_vac = c/nu; m_equiv = E_gamma/c^2; T_equiv = E_gamma/k_B
assumptions: The radiation is represented by one photon of the stated cyclic frequency
The wavelength is a vacuum wavelength
No uncertainty for the input frequency is supplied or propagated
finding.establishes: For an evaluated stated frequency, values satisfying the four displayed identities to finite floating-point precision.
finding.doesNotEstablish: Photon rest mass, a photon rest frame, a thermodynamic state, exact spectral-band boundaries, source-frequency accuracy, or empirical validation.
